en.intro: Arjuna asked what a steady person looks like. Krishna answers by pointing to the exact moment this change happens. Listen for the word that marks this inner turning point.
en.notice: This verse answers Arjuna's question by showing the exact moment wisdom begins. The word yada, when, marks the inner turning point. When all desires are released, the person is no longer driven by the mind, but satisfied by the self.
en.next: Krishna then lists the outer marks of this state: the sage is unshaken by sorrow and free from craving in joy.
en.meaning: The divine says: When a person gives up all desires that arise in the mind, and is satisfied in the true self by the true self alone, that person is called steady in wisdom.

hi.intro: अर्जुन ने पूछा कि स्थितप्रज्ञ के लक्षण क्या हैं, तो श्रीकृष्ण उस सटीक पल की ओर इशारा करते हैं जब यह बदलाव होता है। ध्यान से सुनिए।
hi.meaning: श्रीभगवान कहते हैं: हे पार्थ, जब मनुष्य मन में उठने वाली सारी कामनाओं को पूरी तरह छोड़ देता है और अपने-आप से अपने-आप में ही संतुष्ट रहता है, तब वह स्थितप्रज्ञ कहलाता है।
hi.notice: जो मन की सब कामनाएँ छोड़कर अपने-आप में संतुष्ट है, वह स्थितप्रज्ञ
hi.next: इसके बाद श्रीकृष्ण इस अवस्था के बाहरी लक्षण बताते हैं: ज्ञानी पुरुष दुःख से विचलित नहीं होता और सुख में भी लालसा से मुक्त रहता है।

en.intro: Arjuna asked what a steady person looks like. Krishna answers by pointing to the exact moment this change happens. Listen for the word that marks this inner turning point.
en.body: The divine says: When a person gives up all desires that arise in the mind, and is satisfied in the true self by the true self alone, that person is called steady in wisdom. This verse answers Arjuna's question by showing the exact moment wisdom begins. The word yada, when, marks the inner turning point. When all desires are released, the person is no longer driven by the mind, but satisfied by the self. Krishna then lists the outer marks of this state: the sage is unshaken by sorrow and free from craving in joy.

issues: borrowed: "The steady-minded sage is unshaken by sorrow, free from craving in joy, and beyond attachment, fear, and anger." (This is a direct summary of the NEXT verse (2.56), not this verse (2.55), and is presented in the English 'next' field.)

meaning_changed: "When all desires are released, the person is no longer driven by the mind, but satisfied by the self." (This introduces a contrast ('but') that is not in the source. The source states the person is satisfied in the self (आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः), not that they are 'no longer driven by the mind' as a contrasting alternative. It also adds the unsupported claim that the person is 'no longer driven by the mind'.)

unsupported: "When all desires are released, the person is no longer driven by the mind" (The source text does not state that the person is 'no longer driven by the mind' (मनोगतान् is only used as an adjective for desires, not as a statement about the person's state of being driven).)

wrong_fact: "This verse answers Arjuna's question by showing the exact moment wisdom begins." (This is a factual error about the content of the verse. The verse (2.55) describes the inner state of a steady-minded person (self-satisfaction, giving up desires), not the exact moment wisdom 'begins'. The exact moment of transition is not what this verse states.)

wrong_fact: "Krishna then lists the outer marks of this state: the sage is unshaken by sorrow and free from craving in joy." (This misdescribes the next verse. Verse 56 lists the outer marks (unshaken by sorrow, free from craving, etc.), but the phrase 'Krishna then lists' implies a direct continuation of the current verse's meaning, which is incorrect.)

wrong_fact: "Krishna then lists the outer marks of this state: the sage is unshaken by sorrow and free from craving in joy." (This is the content of verse 56 (the NEXT verse), not verse 55. It is incorrectly attributed to the current verse.)
